All-relevant feature selection with Boruta

Source: R/fs_boruta.R
fs_boruta.Rd

Runs the Boruta algorithm to find every feature that carries information about the target, then optionally prunes correlated features and caps how many are returned. Boruta compares each feature's random-forest importance with that of "shadow" copies of the predictors whose values have been shuffled, and confirms the features that beat the best shadow more often than chance allows.

Usage

fs_boruta(
  data,
  target,
  maxRuns = 250,
  cutoff_features = NULL,
  cutoff_cor = 0.7,
  resolve_tentative = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (or data-frame-like object, or matrix). Predictor columns may be numeric, factor, character, logical, Date, or POSIXt; character and logical columns become factors, Date and POSIXt columns become numeric, and any other type is an error. Neither the target nor the predictors may contain missing values, because Boruta's random forest cannot fit them. Column names must be unique and non-empty, and data must hold at least one predictor besides the target.

target

Name of the target column in data. A factor target means classification and a numeric target means regression; any other type is an error, as is a target with NA or infinite values. Unused factor levels are dropped, and a factor target with fewer than two observed classes is an error.

maxRuns

Maximum number of Boruta iterations: a whole number of at least 11, the minimum Boruta itself accepts. Default 250.

cutoff_features

Optional whole number capping how many features are returned. The top features by median Boruta importance are kept, after any correlation pruning. Default NULL (no cap).

cutoff_cor

Correlation cutoff between 0 and 1 for pruning redundant features from the selected set (see Details). Within a correlated group the feature with the highest median Boruta importance is kept. Only numeric predictors are compared; factor predictors are never pruned. Set NULL to skip pruning. Default 0.7.

resolve_tentative

Logical. If TRUE (default), apply Boruta::TentativeRoughFix() and return only confirmed features. If FALSE, tentative features are included in the selected set.

seed

Optional single whole number within the range of an R integer; fractional or out-of-range values are an error. The seed is applied locally and the previous RNG state is restored on exit. Default NULL: the RNG is never seeded unless you ask.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, report progress, which sets Boruta's doTrace = 1 (decisions are reported as they are made), and name any features dropped by correlation pruning. FALSE (default) sets doTrace = 0.

Value

An object of class fs_result with:

selected

Character vector of selected feature names, after any correlation pruning and cutoff_features cap.

scores

Named numeric vector of median Boruta importance for every candidate feature (NA for a feature with no importance history).

method

"boruta".

task

"classification" for a factor target, "regression" for a numeric one.

model

The Boruta object, after Boruta::TentativeRoughFix() when resolve_tentative = TRUE and some feature was still tentative.

details

A list with boruta_obj (the same Boruta object as model), decisions (the per-feature Confirmed, Tentative, or Rejected factor, after any tentative fix), dropped_correlated (features removed by correlation pruning, empty when cutoff_cor is NULL), and n_features (the number of candidate features).

call

The matched call.

Details

Boruta is an all-relevant selector: it looks for every feature that carries information about the target, rather than the smallest subset that predicts best. Redundant but informative features are therefore all confirmed, which helps you understand a dataset more than it helps you build a compact model. The search costs up to maxRuns random-forest fits, and its outcome varies from run to run unless seed is supplied. The forests are grown on a single thread (num.threads = 1 is passed to Boruta's importance source), in line with featR's sequential default.

Features still undecided when maxRuns is reached are Tentative. resolve_tentative = TRUE settles them with the Boruta::TentativeRoughFix() heuristic, not with further evidence. The heuristic confirms a tentative feature whenever its median importance beats the median importance of the best shadow, a weaker test than the one that confirms features during the run, so it trades false negatives for false positives. In a simulation of 20 data sets with one real predictor and three pure-noise predictors (150 rows, 100 runs), Boruta alone confirmed 5 percent of the noise predictors and 8.3 percent after the rough fix. When false positives are costly, use resolve_tentative = FALSE and inspect details$decisions, or raise maxRuns so fewer features stay tentative.

Two featR steps then run on Boruta's selection, in this order, and both rank features by median Boruta importance:

  1. Correlation pruning (cutoff_cor, on by default at 0.7). Starting from the most important selected feature, every remaining numeric feature whose absolute Pearson correlation with it exceeds cutoff_cor is dropped; the walk then moves to the next most important survivor. Factor predictors are never pruned. A constant column has an undefined correlation, which is treated as 0 with a warning.

  2. The cap (cutoff_features), which keeps the top features by median importance.

See also

The Wrapper methods guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("Boruta", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- data.frame(
    y  = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 20)),
    x1 = rep(c(0, 1), each = 20) + seq(0, 1, length.out = 40),
    x2 = seq_len(40) %% 3
  )
  res <- fs_boruta(d, "y", maxRuns = 25, cutoff_cor = NULL, seed = 42)
  res$selected
  res$scores
}
#>          x1          x2 
#>  1.60306444 -0.07368859 
# }
